response:
Because the blimp is sitting on a curved arch, its upward (buoyant) force is being resolved against a sloped surface. The arch’s rim/contact normal isn’t perfectly vertical, so when the blimp rises it gets a horizontal push as well as a vertical one — which makes it depart at an angle. Small placement overlap or the game’s collision-correction can add a tiny sideways nudge, too.

Fixes: place the blimp centered on a flat platform (or move it slightly so it sits on the topmost point of the arch), or use a flat object under it so it can rise straight up.

3. Move the fan so its front is pointing into open space (not flush against the yellow platform/wall) — if the fan is pressed against a surface the airflow will be blocked.  
4. Start the run (press Play) — electrical devices only run when the puzzle is playing.

One of those will fix it.

ground_truth: The description is wrong the electric motor is powered by the solar panel
response:
Because the panel isn’t actually producing power. In TIM2 a solar panel only outputs electricity when it is receiving light on its sun‑facing side and has a continuous electrical connection to the load. In your setup the flashlight is shining at the panel from the side (and/or the small yellow outlet/switch between the panel and motor is interrupting the circuit), so the panel isn’t lit/connected.

Fixes:
- Shine a light onto the sun‑facing surface (place the lamp/flashlight above or point it down onto the panel) or rotate the panel so the light hits the correct side.
- Remove or flip any electrical switch/outlet between the panel and motor so the connection is on.
- Make sure the panel and motor (or outlet) are touching so there is a continuous electrical contact.
